name: Ege Akgün
intro: Applied Mathematics & Computer Science at UC Berkeley.
interests: Mathematical reasoning, machine learning, and cryptography.

projects.title: Evaluating frontier mathematics
projects.role: Team Lead, Frontier Mathematics; AI Mathematics Expert
projects.summary: Evaluation standards, proof adjudication, and leadership of a 190-person team of IMO medalists.
contribution: Led a 190-person team composed entirely of IMO medalists and managed 8 direct reports on a multimillion-dollar frontier AI mathematics research project for leading frontier AI labs.
Architected evaluation standards for novel, frontier-level mathematics problems and served as the lead arbiter for ambiguous proofs and model-generated reasoning.
projects.challenge: The work required adjudicating ambiguous proofs and model-generated reasoning while enforcing research-grade correctness.
projects.outcome: Evaluation standards and proof adjudication for a frontier AI mathematics research project, alongside the coordination of a large specialist team.
projects.scope: Mercor: August 2025–July 2026. Team Lead, Frontier Mathematics: August 2025–March 2026.

projects.title: Leakage-controlled portfolio research
projects.summary: An eight-asset forecasting and backtesting framework with chronological validation and transaction costs.
contribution: Built a leakage-controlled cryptocurrency forecasting and backtesting framework across eight assets using PyTorch LSTMs, logistic regression, and constrained mean-variance optimization.
Evaluated strategies out of sample under transaction costs using Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, and drawdown metrics.
projects.challengeTitle: The challenge: keeping the test genuinely out of sample
projects.challenge: Chronological train, validation, and test splits separate fitting from model selection and final evaluation. Scalers are fitted on training observations; hyperparameters and decision thresholds are selected on validation data. Position changes incur fees and slippage.
projects.outcome: In the reference test, the LSTM had a smaller maximum drawdown than BTC buy-and-hold, but lower return and Sharpe. This is one test regime; it does not establish consistent outperformance.
projects.scope: Reference test: August 2024–July 2025. One-way fees plus slippage: 15 basis points. Dataset downloaded September 3, 2026.
projects.limitations: Daily close-to-close data and a single market regime limit the conclusions. Short borrow costs, market impact, funding rates, and tax effects are not modeled. Eight assets introduce universe-selection risk.

projects.title: Computing on encrypted data
projects.summary: A Legendre-symbol-based partially homomorphic encryption prototype in Python and SageMath.
contribution: Designed and prototyped a Legendre-symbol-based partially homomorphic encryption scheme in Python/SageMath for computation on encrypted healthcare data.
Selected at age 14 as one of three high-school researchers; studied graduate-level cryptography and worked with senior cryptographers during a three-year internship.
projects.challengeTitle: The research problem: computation on encrypted data
projects.challenge: The project explored a partially homomorphic encryption scheme for computation on encrypted healthcare data, connecting mathematical cryptography with a working prototype.
projects.scope: National Research Institute of Electronics and Cryptology, Kocaeli, Türkiye. September 2022–June 2025.

projects.title: Building a mathematics community
projects.summary: Co-organizing a national olympiad mathematics program, selecting students, and teaching advanced mathematics.
contribution: Co-led a highly selective national olympiad mathematics program, delivering 50+ advanced lectures and selecting and training 200+ students from 5,000+ applicants—an approximately 4% selection rate.
projects.challengeTitle: The work: selection and advanced instruction
projects.challenge: The role combined co-organizing the program, selecting students from a national applicant pool, and delivering advanced olympiad mathematics lectures.
projects.outcome: The program selected and trained more than 200 students from over 5,000 applicants. My contribution included co-organization and more than 50 advanced lectures.
projects.scope: Türkiye, 2023–2025. Program-level student and applicant counts; shared organizing responsibility.

projects.title: Reinforcement learning & the Four Color Theorem
projects.summary: Investigating a two-player game formulation of D-reducibility and simpler proof certificates.
contribution: Conducting research under Prof. Olga Holtz, working with Marco David and Dan Romik on reinforcement learning for the Four Color Theorem.
Investigating a two-player game formulation of D-reducibility to uncover structure in computer-assisted proofs and explore simpler proof certificates using machine learning.
projects.challenge: Can a two-player game formulation of D-reducibility help uncover structure in computer-assisted proofs and support simpler proof certificates?
projects.scope: UC Berkeley. Research in progress; this page describes the question being investigated.
